citation: (1) Theory of Constraints Institute, 'Five Focusing Steps', https://www.tocinstitute.org/five-focusing-steps.html (undated). (2) Wikipedia, 'Theory of constraints', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory_of_constraints, citing Cox & Goldratt (1986) The Goal, North River Press; Goldratt & Fox (1986) The Race; Goldratt (1990) The Haystack Syndrome. (3) TOCI home page https://www.tocinstitute.org/theory-of-constraints.html.
source_tier: Practitioner/vendor organisation page (TOC Institute) plus encyclopedia (Wikipedia, secondary). Neither is The Goal itself.
access_status: TOCI five-focusing-steps page and Wikipedia page fetched and read via summarising fetch tool (Wikipedia: first 100,000 of 110,926 characters). The Goal and Haystack Syndrome were NOT opened. TOCI 'The Goal Summary' page not opened. [uncertain]
sponsor_and_incentive: TOC Institute sells TOC training and certification, so it has an incentive to promote TOC. Wikipedia has no sponsor.
exact_quotes: TOCI (five-focusing-steps page, headings): 'IDENTIFY the system's constraint'; 'EXPLOIT the constraint'; 'SUBORDINATE everything else to the constraint'; 'ELEVATE the constraint'; 'PREVENT INERTIA from becoming the constraint'. TOCI origin anecdote: a reporter asked Goldratt to summarise TOC in a sentence; he answered with one word, 'FOCUS!'. Wikipedia, Five Focusing Steps section: 'Identify the system's constraint(s).'; 'Decide how to exploit the system's constraint(s).'; 'Subordinate everything else to the above decision.'; 'Elevate the system's constraint(s).'; 'Warning! If in the previous steps a constraint has been broken, go back to step 1, but do not allow inertia to cause a system's constraint.' Wikipedia, DBR section: 'The rope is the work release mechanism for the plant.' Drum: 'the rate at which the physical constraint of the plant can work.' Orders released 'at one buffer time before they are due to be processed by the constraint.'
key_claims: Five steps: identify the constraint, exploit it (get the most from it with what you have), subordinate everything else to that decision, elevate it (add capacity), then repeat and do not let inertia become the constraint. Step 5 is a loop, not a separate action: the TOCI wording is 'prevent inertia', Wikipedia's is 'go back to step 1'. Wikipedia attributes the theory to Goldratt's The Goal (1984 per text; citation is the 1986 Cox & Goldratt edition). Drum-buffer-rope: drum is the constraint's pace, buffer protects the constraint from starvation (measured in time), rope releases work to the shop floor so upstream does not outrun the constraint. Wikipedia cites The Race (1986) and The Haystack Syndrome (1990) for DBR.
headline_figures: None. No numbers in the sources beyond dates (The Goal 1984/1986; The Race 1986; Haystack Syndrome 1990). Not applicable to the user's lead.
sample_and_method: Not empirical. Conceptual management framework, originally developed in manufacturing scheduling and presented in Goldratt's business novel The Goal.
limitations: Neither source is The Goal. Which book first stated the five steps in exactly this form is not confirmed (Wikipedia gives The Goal; step wording differs between TOCI and Wikipedia). Sources describe manufacturing; application to knowledge work or AI code review is an extrapolation. Step 5 wording varies by version. [uncertain] The claim that the rope is the 'original subordination mechanism' is not stated in either source: Wikipedia ties subordination to step 3 and describes the rope only as work release; this is an inference, though a reasonable one. TOCI page says it does not name DBR or 'rope' at all.
what_a_leader_can_do: Apply the sequence to review: name the review step as the constraint, get more from it without new capacity (prioritise, shrink changes, stop wasting reviewer time), then subordinate upstream work (limit how much AI-generated work is released, which is the rope's job) before adding reviewers or tooling (elevate). Evidence is conceptual and from manufacturing; strength for AI code review specifically is weak and untested here.
overlap_with_site_essays: Overlaps with Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part and The Verification Gap (verification as limited capacity); little overlap with Checking Isn't Catching or What It Takes to Trust Agent Output beyond the idea that throttling input matters.
